files_changed.summary: Counting semaphore (TryAcquire/Release) for MaxConcurrentRuns admission control (§7.7).

Supervisor.Go starts a tracked, panic-recovering goroutine derived from the caller's ctx with its own internally-owned cancel func; Shutdown cancels every tracked context and blocks until they drain or its own ctx deadline passes -- the only sanctioned owner of a goroutine that outlives its caller's stack frame (§7.1 rule 1, §7.10).
Updated package doc comment from 'Not yet implemented' now that Semaphore and Supervisor exist.
-race tests: fn runs, panic recovery doesn't crash the process, Shutdown cancels tracked contexts and drains, Shutdown respects its own deadline when fn ignores cancellation, concurrent Go+Shutdown.

RunEventType enum + RunEvent struct -- the concrete Hub.Publish payload shape hub.go's own comment deferred to 'once orchestrator.go actually publishes to a Hub'. JSON tags included for task 012's future SSE marshaling.

Orchestrator.Run(ctx, runID): publishes run.started, runs Start+Advance to the analytic stage, checks ctx.Done() before the LLM call (run.cancelled path), runs the existing runAnalytic stub, publishes stage.completed{analytic} or run.failed, and recovers any panic into a run.failed event + Fail(). Deliberately does not loop over a stages.Registry() or publish run.completed -- see analyze.json open_questions for why.

NewService now takes hub, supervisor, maxConcurrentRuns, maxRunDuration (with <=0 defaults, mirroring NewHub's pattern). StartRun keeps only content validation synchronous on reqCtx; everything else moved into Orchestrator.Run, dispatched via RunContext(reqCtx, budget) + supervisor.Go, gated by a TryAcquire semaphore (over-limit runs are admitted pending, no goroutine started). Added createRun/mutateRun/setPoints/contentFor as the lock-protected internal surface Orchestrator uses instead of touching the runs map directly. RunState now returns a *Run snapshot copy (not the live mutable pointer) so a caller reading fields after the call can never race with the orchestrator goroutine.

Rewritten for the async contract. fakeLLM gained gate/started/wantPanic modes for sleep-free synchronization. Added waitForTerminal (subscribes to the hub, drains replay then live until a terminal event) as the one synchronization primitive every test built on. Replaced the old synchronous StartRun assertions with 9 tests covering g1/g2 (detached context, caller-cancel-after-return), g4 (panic recovery), g5 (event sequence for success/failure), g6 (late-subscriber replay), g7 (MaxConcurrentRuns queuing), plus the original success/error/empty-content cases updated to the new hub-driven synchronization.

Added MaxRunDuration (default 15m, matching §7.5's own worked example) and MaxConcurrentRuns (default 24, matching §7.9's worked budget) fields, set as literals in Load() the same way every other bound in this file already is (ShutdownTimeout, MembershipCacheTTL, etc.) -- not env-parsed, consistent with existing style.

decisions: Orchestrator holds *Service and *Hub, constructed once inside NewService (s.orchestrator = NewOrchestrator(s, hub)) rather than being passed in separately by the caller -- keeps StartRun's call site a single s.orchestrator.Run(ctx, id) and avoids a second public constructor callers would need to keep in sync with Service's own dependencies.

Supervisor.Go derives its own context.WithCancel(ctx) internally and stores that cancel func in its registry, rather than requiring the caller to pass a cancel func alongside fn -- reconciles the 011 prompt's Go(ctx, fn) signature with its own requirement that Shutdown can signal tracked runs 'via each entry's stored cancel func' (see analyze.json risks for why this reading was necessary, not just a preference).

Content is stored per-run in the in-memory runRecord (set once at createRun, read once by Orchestrator via contentFor) rather than threaded through Orchestrator.Run's signature -- keeps Run(ctx, runID) matching the 011 prompt's literal signature and matches how a later multi-stage orchestrator would read prior-stage output from the run record rather than a raw string parameter.

RunState returns a copied *Run (dereferenced struct copy re-boxed as a pointer) instead of the record's live pointer -- the live pointer is mutated by the orchestrator goroutine under s.mu, and handing it out would let a caller read fields after the lock is released with no synchronization, which -race would (correctly) flag the moment a test read RunState concurrently with an in-flight run.

No queue-drain worker was added for runs admitted over MaxConcurrentRuns -- they stay 'pending' forever once queued in this task's implementation. §7.7 only specifies the admission response ('queue the run, return 202'), not a drain mechanism, and adding one would be scope invention beyond what any goal in task.json asks for; documented as a known gap in analyze.json risks rather than silently pretended to be complete.
